ModMetaData.name: RimMandrake: Explosive Plant Growth
ModMetaData.author: mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
EXPLOSIVE_PLANT_GROWTH_1. Plants grow fast every day, and water-soaked plants grow where you can watch them — and every soaked plant is a countdown.
Ships inside RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes as one of its engines (it has its own toggle on the Baroque Biomes settings page, and its own settings page). RM tier: nothing here knows what campaign or planet uses it.
EVERYDAY GROWTH (PLANT_GROWTH_MERGE_NEVER_MEANT_APART: the former Jawa Plant Growth, mandrake.rut.plantgrowth, fused in 2026-10-16). Plants grow faster every day, no water needed: wild plants and crops x4, trees x2.5; the wet jungles (Greentide, Miasma, Fever Wood) x10, trees x6.25, instead; stalled biomes a roster names x0.4 instead. Exactly one band applies; the soak multiplies on top. It scales the composite growth rate, so light, temperature and fertility still apply. Anima, gauranlen, ambrosia, a roster's bandExemptPlants and plants under a grow-day are left alone. Every number is a Mod Settings slider.
WHERE. Both tiers run only on maps whose biome Baroque Biomes ships, for every plant growing there. An option (off by default, UNSUPPORTED and untested) extends them to every biome; a campaign layer's roster can do the same for its whole world (scopeAllBiomes).
THE SOAK. Ground becomes SOAKED when qualifying fresh water arrives in quantity, and dries back over hours to a day. Routes: a flood pushed in by another mod (RimMandrake: Flooded Canyon), irrigation (a dug FlowWorks channel holding fresh water soaks the ground beside it — rivers and lakes never do), a salt-line surge's fresh side (Environmental Hazards' gradient axis), and any weather a roster names as soaking. Soaked plants grow x10 ON TOP of the everyday band. Salt, fungus, and plants whose slowness is a mechanic (anima, gauranlen, ambrosia) never soak.
THE CHARGE. A soaked plant that reaches full size keeps going: it swells past natural size, and it tells you, in a fixed order — the ground darkens and sprouts, it swells, its hue shifts wrong, it trembles, it creaks, and then it goes silent. Then the top.
THE TOP belongs to the PLANT, never the ground it stands on: - Churn (the default): it splits, dies, drops its produce and sows a ring of sprouts that keep going. It respects your floors and walls. - Burst (dry-adapted plants only): a pop, chaff, bruises and knockdown nearby (never lethal on its own), premium produce scattered — and a sown ring that ignores your zones, floors and doorways. - Tinder: a burst whose debris is fuel. - Slime: the ring turns the ground to slime. - Rupture (contaminated plants): a gas cloud, spawned things, sprouts, and mutations for anyone in the cloud without a full vacuum seal. - Flush (giant trees): it swells inside and survives, silently.
PLAYER VERBS. Harvest a swollen plant for extra produce. Cut it to defuse it — though once it trembles, the last swing is a gamble. Keep ground dry. Grazing animals (and a dry-air blower, where another mod ships one) suppress encroachment for a few days.
Every mechanic has a Mod Settings toggle; defaults are the shipped behaviour. Plant tops are data: an RM_ExplosiveGrowthRosterDef (by name, silently skipping absent plants) or an RM_ExplosiveGrowthExtension on a plant you own. Soak/suppress are exposed as RimMandrake.ExplosiveGrowth.ExplosiveGrowthAPI; the Baroque Biomes members (Flooded Canyon, Environmental Hazards) call it directly, other mods may call it by reflection.
Ships the IncidentWorker behind a map-scale bloom (RM_IncidentWorker_BloomBurst); a campaign layer names the IncidentDef and the bloom plant.
The performance gate (TPS on a jungle-density map under a full-map soak) is OWED to a live session; no density is promised until it runs.
